headline: Segment growth continues, but a higher tax rate caps profit
summary_short: Fiscal Q4 revenue rose 7.2% y/y to $2,231.8M as all three segments grew, but a jump in the effective tax rate to 23.9% from 12.9% held net income to $221.2M, down 2.0% y/y despite operating income up 8.9%.
summary_long: RPM's fiscal Q4 (three months ended May 31, 2026) revenue rose 7.2% y/y to $2,231.8M and 38.8% q/q. For the full fiscal year, consolidated net sales rose 6.7% to $7,863.4M as CPG, PCG and Consumer segments all grew, driven by roofing/systems, turnkey flooring and India/Middle East demand, partly offset by Consumer's organic DIY/European softness. Full-year gross margin held flat at 41.4% as cost inflation and MAP 2025 plant-consolidation costs offset pricing and procurement savings. SG&A rose $141.6M on acquisitions, healthcare costs and a $9.7M impairment. The effective tax rate jumped to 23.9% from 12.9%, capping full-year net income at $662.5M (-4.0% y/y) despite income before taxes up 9.8%. Operating cash flow rose to $898.7M; capex was $223.5M.

drivers.explanation: All three segments grew net sales for the full fiscal year and operating cash flow improved, but a normalized effective tax rate (23.9% vs 12.9%) capped net income and EPS growth despite higher income before taxes.

CPG grew on roofing/systems for high-performance buildings and concrete admixtures; PCG grew on turnkey flooring, protective/fireproofing coatings and strength in India/Middle East; Consumer grew via acquisitions despite an organic DIY/European decline.

Full-year gross margin was flat at 41.4% as cost inflation, tariff impacts and MAP 2025 plant-consolidation inefficiencies were offset by pricing actions and MAP 2025 procurement and manufacturing savings.
SG&A rose $141.6 million on acquisitions, healthcare costs, merit increases and a $9.7 million impairment charge, partly offset by a $14.4 million earn-out gain and MAP 2025 / restructuring savings.
Full-year net income fell despite income before taxes rising 9.8%, because the effective tax rate normalized to 23.9% from an unusually low 12.9% a year earlier.
